practice.title: Practice: a note from the library

sentences.original: The central library will be closed for scheduled maintenance on Saturday, and all borrowed items may be returned via the external drop box.
sentences.light: The main library will be closed for planned repairs on Saturday, and you can return borrowed items in the outside drop box.
sentences.simple: The main library is closed on Saturday for repairs. You can still return books. Use the drop box outside.
sentences.very_simple: The library is closed on Saturday. Use the box outside to return books.

sentences.original: Patrons wishing to renew their membership should do so prior to the expiry date in order to retain borrowing privileges.
sentences.light: Members who want to renew should do it before the end date so they can keep borrowing books.
sentences.simple: Do you want to keep borrowing books? Renew your membership before it ends.
sentences.very_simple: Renew your card before it ends. Then you can keep borrowing.

sentences.original: Late fees of 5 rupees per day are applicable to overdue items.
sentences.light: Late items cost 5 rupees for each day they are late.
sentences.simple: Is a book late? You pay 5 rupees for each late day.
sentences.very_simple: Late books cost 5 rupees a day.

glossary.expiry date: The date something stops being valid.

questions.q: On which day is the library closed?
How much is the late fee?

leaflet.title: Medicine leaflet: Lisinor 10 mg tablets
leaflet.note: Fictional medicine, written for this study. Not medical advice.

sentences.original: Lisinor 10 mg tablets are indicated for the treatment of hypertension in adults.
sentences.light: Lisinor 10 mg tablets are used to treat high blood pressure in adults.
sentences.simple: Lisinor 10 mg tablets treat high blood pressure. They are for adults.
sentences.very_simple: This medicine is Lisinor 10 mg. It lowers high blood pressure. It is for adults.

sentences.original: The recommended dosage is one tablet administered orally once daily, preferably at the same time each morning.
sentences.light: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, ideally at the same time each morning.
sentences.simple: Take one tablet by mouth once a day. Try to take it at the same time each morning.
sentences.very_simple: Take one tablet a day. Swallow it. Take it every morning.

sentences.original: Do not exceed the prescribed dose; if you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for your next dose.
sentences.light: Do not take more than your prescribed dose. If you miss a dose, take it when you remember, unless your next dose is due soon.
sentences.simple: Never take more than your doctor said. Did you forget a tablet? Take it when you remember. But if the next one is due soon, skip the missed one.
sentences.very_simple: Do not take extra tablets. Forgot one? Take it when you remember. Is the next one due soon? Then skip it.

sentences.original: Concomitant use with potassium supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics may result in elevated serum potassium levels.
sentences.light: Taking it with potassium supplements or certain water tablets may raise the potassium in your blood.
sentences.simple: Taking it with potassium pills or some water tablets can raise the potassium in your blood.
sentences.very_simple: Potassium pills can cause a problem with this medicine. So can some water tablets. They raise potassium in your blood.

sentences.original: Common adverse effects include dizziness, headache and a persistent dry cough, affecting up to 1 in 10 people.
sentences.light: Common side effects are dizziness, headache and a dry cough that does not go away. Up to 1 in 10 people get them.
sentences.simple: It may make you dizzy. It may give you a headache. It may cause a dry cough that lasts. Up to 1 in 10 people get these.
sentences.very_simple: You may feel dizzy. Your head may hurt. You may get a dry cough. Up to 1 in 10 people get this.

sentences.original: Discontinue use and seek immediate medical attention if you experience difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, or severe skin reactions.
sentences.light: Stop taking it and get medical help right away if you have trouble breathing, a swollen face, or bad skin reactions.
sentences.simple: Stop the medicine right away if you cannot breathe well. Stop if your face swells. Stop if your skin is very sore. Call a doctor now.
sentences.very_simple: Stop the medicine. Call a doctor now if you cannot breathe. Call now if your face swells. Call now if your skin hurts badly.

sentences.original: Consult your physician before use if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if you have a history of renal or hepatic impairment.
sentences.light: Talk to your doctor before taking it if you are pregnant, planning a baby or breastfeeding, or if you have had kidney or liver problems.
sentences.simple: Ask your doctor first if you are pregnant or want a baby. Ask first if you are breastfeeding. Ask first if you have had kidney or liver problems.
sentences.very_simple: Pregnant? Ask your doctor first. Want a baby? Ask first. Breastfeeding? Ask first. Kidney or liver problems? Ask first.

sentences.original: Store below 25°C in the original packaging and keep out of the sight and reach of children.
sentences.light: Keep it below 25°C in its box, where children cannot see or reach it.
sentences.simple: Keep it below 25°C. Keep it in its box. Keep it away from children.
sentences.very_simple: Keep it cool, below 25 degrees. Keep it in the box. Keep it away from children.

glossary.indicated for: Used for; what the medicine is meant to treat.
glossary.dosage: How much medicine to take, and how often.
glossary.prescribed: Ordered for you by a doctor.
glossary.concomitant: At the same time. Here: taking two medicines together.
glossary.potassium: A mineral in your blood. Too much can harm your heart.
glossary.potassium-sparing diuretics: Water tablets that keep potassium in your body.
glossary.serum: The liquid part of your blood.
glossary.adverse effects: Side effects; unwanted effects of a medicine.
glossary.impairment: When a part of the body does not work well.

questions.q: How many tablets should you take each day?
What should you do if your face swells?
options: Stop the medicine and get medical help now

questions.q: Which of these may be a problem to take with this medicine?
Below what temperature should you store it?

bank.title: Bank letter: update your KYC documents
bank.note: Fictional letter written for this study.

sentences.original: We are writing to inform you that, pursuant to a periodic review of your account, your KYC documentation requires re-verification.
sentences.light: We are writing to tell you that, after a regular check of your account, we need to check your identity documents again.
sentences.simple: We checked your account, as we do from time to time. We need to check your ID papers again.
sentences.very_simple: We need to check your ID again. This is a normal check.

sentences.original: Failure to submit the requisite documents by 15 March 2026 will result in the temporary suspension of debit transactions on your account.
sentences.light: If you do not send the needed documents by 15 March 2026, you will not be able to take money out of your account for a while.
sentences.simple: Send the papers by 15 March 2026. If you do not, you cannot take money out of your account for a while.
sentences.very_simple: Send your papers by 15 March 2026. If not, you cannot take out money for some time.

sentences.original: Credits to the account, including salary and pension, will continue to be processed during any period of suspension.
sentences.light: Money coming into the account, like salary and pension, will still be added during this time.
sentences.simple: Money can still come in during this time. Your salary and pension will still arrive.
sentences.very_simple: Money can still come in. Your salary and pension still arrive.

sentences.original: Acceptable documents comprise a valid Aadhaar card, passport, or voter identity card, together with a recent photograph.
sentences.light: You can send a valid Aadhaar card, passport or voter ID card, along with a recent photo.
sentences.simple: Send an Aadhaar card, a passport, or a voter ID card. Also send a recent photo.
sentences.very_simple: Send one ID card. Aadhaar, passport or voter ID is fine. Add a new photo.

sentences.original: Documents may be submitted at any branch, or electronically via the mobile banking application under Profile, then Update KYC.
sentences.light: You can hand in the documents at any branch, or online in the mobile banking app under Profile, then Update KYC.
sentences.simple: You can go to any branch. Or you can use the bank app. In the app, go to Profile, then Update KYC.
sentences.very_simple: Go to any branch. Or use the bank app. Tap Profile. Then tap Update KYC.

sentences.original: Please note that the bank will never request your PIN, password or one-time passcode by telephone or email.
sentences.light: Please note: the bank will never ask for your PIN, password or one-time code by phone or email.
sentences.simple: The bank will never ask for your PIN or password. It will never ask for a one-time code. Not by phone, and not by email.
sentences.very_simple: We never ask for your PIN. We never ask for your password or code. Not by phone. Not by email.

sentences.original: For assistance, contact our helpline on 1800 425 0018, available 24 hours a day.
sentences.light: For help, call our helpline on 1800 425 0018, open 24 hours a day.
sentences.simple: Need help? Call 1800 425 0018. It is open 24 hours a day.
sentences.very_simple: Need help? Call 1800 425 0018. Call any time, 24 hours a day.

glossary.periodic review: A check the bank does from time to time.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: the bank checking who you are.
glossary.re-verification: Checking again that something is correct.
glossary.debit transactions: Money going out of your account, like cash withdrawals and payments.
glossary.electronically: Online, using a phone or computer.
glossary.one-time passcode: A short code sent to you that works only once.

questions.q: By what date must you send your documents?
What still works if your account is paused?
Will the bank ever ask for your PIN by phone?

bill.title: Electricity bill notice
bill.note: Fictional bill written for this study.

sentences.original: Your electricity bill for the billing period 1 September to 30 September amounts to ₹2,340, inclusive of applicable taxes.
sentences.light: Your electricity bill for 1 September to 30 September is ₹2,340, including taxes.
sentences.simple: Your power bill is ₹2,340. It covers 1 September to 30 September. Tax is included.
sentences.very_simple: You owe ₹2,340 for power. This is for 1 September to 30 September. Tax is in it.

sentences.original: Payment must be remitted on or before 20 October to avoid a late payment surcharge of 2% of the outstanding amount.
sentences.light: Pay on or before 20 October to avoid a late fee of 2% of the amount you owe.
sentences.simple: Pay by 20 October. Do not pay late. If you do, you pay 2% extra.
sentences.very_simple: Pay by 20 October. Late? Then you pay 2% more. Do not be late.

sentences.original: Your consumption of 312 units exceeds the subsidised threshold of 200 units; consequently, units above this limit are charged at the higher slab rate of ₹7.50 per unit.
sentences.light: You used 312 units, which is more than the 200 units that get a lower price, so the extra units cost the higher rate of ₹7.50 each.
sentences.simple: You used 312 units. The first 200 units are cheaper. Each unit above 200 costs ₹7.50.
sentences.very_simple: You used 312 units. The first 200 cost less. Each extra unit costs ₹7.50.

sentences.original: Should the bill remain unpaid for a period exceeding 30 days beyond the due date, the supply may be disconnected without further notice.
sentences.light: If the bill is still unpaid more than 30 days after the due date, your power may be cut off without another warning.
sentences.simple: Do not leave the bill unpaid for more than 30 days after the due date. If you do, your power may be cut off. You may get no more warnings.
sentences.very_simple: Pay within 30 days of the due date. If not, your power may be cut. You will get no more warnings.

sentences.original: Payments can be made through the utility's website, authorised UPI applications, or at any designated collection centre.
sentences.light: You can pay on the power company's website, with approved UPI apps, or at any official payment centre.
sentences.simple: You can pay on the website. You can pay with a UPI app. Or you can pay at a payment centre.
sentences.very_simple: Pay on the website. Or pay with a UPI app. Or pay at a centre.

sentences.original: Consumers eligible for the senior citizen rebate of 5% must register their date of birth with the customer care department.
sentences.light: People who can get the 5% discount for senior citizens must give their date of birth to customer care.
sentences.simple: Are you a senior citizen? You may get 5% off. Tell customer care your date of birth to get it.
sentences.very_simple: Older people can get 5% off. Tell customer care your date of birth.

glossary.surcharge: An extra fee added to the bill.
glossary.units: How electricity use is measured. One unit is one kilowatt hour.
glossary.subsidised threshold: The amount you can use at a lower, government-supported price.
glossary.slab rate: The price per unit for that band of use.
glossary.UPI: A way to pay from your phone straight from your bank account.

questions.q: What is the last day to pay without a late fee?
How many units did you use?
How much discount can senior citizens get?
